run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:06:33Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert (reported by Alertmanager for otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:06:33Z) matches a burst of frontend error spans between about 00:06 and 00:14 that is confined to the /api/data path: GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', the client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect all errored with matching counts, while frontend's cart and checkout operations recorded no error spans. The ad Deployment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-18T00:05:22Z (pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5, same image/env/resources), its old pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq was killed at 00:05:25Z and the new pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was created and started by 00:05:24Z. The new ad container then burned its entire 50m CPU limit with 98.5-100% CFS throttling from 00:06 to 00:13, produced no GetAds server spans from about 00:06 to 00:15, and its only log line is 'Ad service starting.' at 00:09:35Z, while frontend kept issuing GetAds calls that hung for more than 15s. frontend-proxy also recorded its own error spans on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' in the same window. The flagd-config ConfigMap holds adManualGc with defaultVariant 'on' ('Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service') while every other fault flag in that file is off; the ad Service was restarted with an unchanged pod template and then failed, so per the fault-setting pattern the ConfigMap holding that setting is the leading root-cause candidate. I could not verify when that value was changed or observe the GC behaviour itself, and the rollout restart itself has no traced trigger, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend's error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was 0 up to 00:05, became non-zero at 00:07 (1.5/s), peaked at about 3.57/s around 00:10, and was 0 again from 00:15 onward.

frontend's error spans are limited to GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect; all other frontend span names queried (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/cart, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) show increase 0.

Deployment otel-demo/ad carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:05:22Z; ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 was created at 00:05:22Z with 1 replica and ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 was scaled to 0, and both ReplicaSets declare the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, identical env and identical resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi).

otel-demo events show the ad rollout: Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz Scheduled 00:05:22Z, image 'already present on machine' 00:05:23Z, container Created 00:05:23Z, Started 00:05:24Z; Pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq Killing at 00:05:25Z; Deployment ad Scale up ad-d89765fb5 0->1 and scale down ad-554b849958 1->0. No other otel-demo workload has rollout events in the window.

ad service server-side GetAds span counts (increase per 5m) fell from 231.1 in 00:00-00:05 to 32.2 in 00:05-00:10, 0 in 00:10-00:15 and 0 in 00:15-00:20, then recovered to 176.6 in 00:20-00:25; at 1-minute resolution the 2-minute increase is 0 for every window ending 00:08 through 00:15 and 78.7 in the window ending 00:16.

frontend's client-side grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans continued throughout the outage (about 66-106 per 1-minute increase window) and became very slow: in the window ending 00:15 there were 69.3 spans, only 28 at or below 1000 ms and 46.7 at or below 15000 ms, i.e. about 41 spans over 1 s and about 22.6 spans over 15 s.

The new ad container ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was pinned at its CPU limit: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total rate rose from 0.0145 to 0.0494 cores (limit 50m = 0.05 cores) and container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total/container_cpu_cfs_periods_total was 0.985-1.0 from 00:06 through 00:13, easing to 0.24 by 00:16; the previous pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq used only 0.0042-0.0049 cores with a throttling ratio of 0.05-0.11.

ad container memory working set grew from 73 MB at 00:06 to 358 MB by about 00:15 and stayed there, under the 450Mi limit, while the old pod sat at a steady ~345 MB; there is no OOM signal for ad (restart count 0, last state empty).
The ad Deployment's container declares CPU limit 50m / memory limit 450Mi and has no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, so the new pod is Ready as soon as the container starts.
The only log line retained for the new ad container is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-18T00:09:35.903Z, and there is no previous container instance for this pod.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) sets adManualGc to defaultVariant 'on' with description 'Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service', while adFailure, adHighCpu, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodpageHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all have defaultVariant 'off'.

The flagd Deployment mounts ConfigMap flagd-config into the flagd container (volume config-ro, mounted at /etc/flagd for the flagd container), so flagd-config is the flag source in effect for the workloads.

frontend-proxy recorded its own error spans in the same interval: span 'ingress' increase 457.9 and span 'router frontend egress' increase 440 in the 10-minute window ending 00:15, and 0 in the window ending 00:25.

A per-service error-span query over 00:00-00:28 returned error series only for frontend (927.8 in the 5-minute window ending 00:10, 797.5 ending 00:15, 0 ending 00:20), frontend-proxy (457.8/418.8/0), fraud-detection (isolated 1.11 and 1.25), and explicit zeros for accounting, ad, payment and recommendation.

The ad service itself recorded no error status: its AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory, getRandomAds and resolve spans all carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET with 0 error increase in 00:00-00:28, and its only error span is a single flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error per 10-minute window, so ad's failure is unavailability/latency rather than returned error responses.

Before the 00:05:22Z restart the ad container ran the same image, env and flag source for over 30 minutes at 0.004 cores with only 5-11% CFS throttling, so the adManualGc flag alone did not produce the CPU saturation observed after the restart; the post-restart state (fresh JVM plus the flag) coincides with it.

All five cluster nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False, including i-00afa9d1463304f93 where the new ad pod ran, so node-level resource pressure is not the source of the ad pod's CPU throttling.

fraud-detection's OOMKilled container (exit code 137, finished 2026-11-17T23:38:17Z, restarts 1) is not the cause of the frontend alert: it predates the error burst, the pod has been running since, and its only error span is the same flagd EventStream error seen at a constant ~1.05-1.10 per 10-minute window before and during the burst.
The fault flags adFailure and adHighCpu are not the cause because both have defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, and there is no ad-side error or CPU-load evidence attributable to them.

Leading root-cause candidate: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holding adManualGc='on' for the ad service. With that forced-GC fault active, the ad rollout restart at 00:05:22Z (unchanged pod template) left the fresh ad container spinning at its 50m CPU limit with ~100% CFS throttling from 00:06 to 00:13, unable to serve GetAds; frontend's /api/data calls to AdService/GetAds hung (about 22.6 spans over 15 s in the window ending 00:15) and errored, producing the frontend RequestErrorRate alert and frontend-proxy ingress errors.

Competing hypothesis: the 00:05:22Z rollout restart alone, with the ad container's 50m CPU limit, made the fresh JVM take about 9 minutes to serve (container started 00:05:24Z, 'Ad service starting.' at 00:09:35Z, spans only after ~00:15), and adManualGc played no role; this remains open because the old pod burned almost no CPU with the same flag file and I could not observe GC activity.

Contributing factor: the ad container has no readiness/startup probe, so the Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad routed frontend GetAds traffic to the new pod while the application was still not listening/serving; this amplified the restart into an approximately 9-minute error window.

Sampled frontend spans from the last available trace window before the burst (about 00:03:06) are all successful (http.status_code 200, rpc.grpc.status_code 0), so the failures begin after the ad rollout, not before it.

Set adManualGc back to 'off' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (and confirm with the fault-injection owner that it was intentionally enabled), then watch ad's CPU/CFS throttling and frontend GetAds error rate for recovery.

Add a readinessProbe (and startupProbe) to the ad Deployment and raise its 50m CPU limit so a starting JVM is not marked ready and throttled to a standstill; consider raising the ad Deployment's replica count to keep a warm replica during rollouts.
Identify who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-18T00:05:22Z using cluster audit logs or change history (that integration is not available in this Run).

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so I cannot tell when adManualGc in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config changed from off to on, nor who or what triggered the ad rollout restart; only the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:05:22Z is visible.

The declared fault itself (full manual garbage collections in the ad service) was not directly observed: the previous ad container's logs are gone with the deleted pod and the current container's log stream returned only 'Ad service starting.' at 00:09:35.903Z.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend in 00:04-00:20; the sampled spans end around 00:03:07, so per-span error messages/status details for the failing GetAds calls during 00:06-00:15 are unavailable.
Prometheus has no rule named RequestErrorRate loaded (list_prometheus_rules returned nothing), so the alert's exact expression and threshold could not be verified.

Error state of services that returned no error series in the per-service query (cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka, load-generator) is unknown, not zero.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count had no series in the query window, so the frontend's HTTP 5xx counts cannot be confirmed from that metric.
The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no objects with status no_data, so absence of network policies is not established.
next_steps: Confirm with the fault-injection owner that adManualGc was deliberately enabled and when, and correlate that with the 00:05:22Z ad rollout restart via cluster audit logs.
Inspect the ad service's GC logs/JVM metrics (or re-run adManualGc=on against a warm pod) to confirm that the flag pins the container at its 50m CPU limit.
Review whether other workloads were restarted at 00:05:22Z outside otel-demo by querying change history once that integration is available.

  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:

    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317

      insecure: true

      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
